column3: NASB renders “Men brothers” as “Brethren,” “lived as a citizen” as “lived my life,” and “good conscience” as “perfectly good conscience.”

NASB renders “insult” as “revile.”
NASB follows the critical text; “I had not known” is rendered “I was not aware.” The quotation is in capitals.
NASB follows the critical text (“was crying out,” “of Pharisees”); “I am judged” is rendered “I am on trial.”
NASB follows the critical text; “crowd” is rendered “assembly.”
NASB follows the critical text; “both” is rendered “them all.”
NASB follows the critical text without the Textus Receptus words “let us not fight against God”; “were contending” is rendered “began to argue heatedly.”
NASB follows the critical text; “troop” is rendered “troops.”
NASB follows the critical text without “Paul”; it renders “the following night” as “the night immediately following” and adds “My cause.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the Jews”).
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “with an oath” as “under a solemn oath” and “to eat” as “to taste.”
NASB follows the critical text without “tomorrow”; it expands “examine more earnestly” as “determine his case by a more thorough investigation” and adds “the place.”
NASB follows the critical text (“ambush”); it adds “their.”
NASB renders “take” as “Lead.”
NASB follows the critical text.
NASB renders “was inquiring” as “began to inquire” and adds “of him.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “somewhat.”
NASB renders “be persuaded” as “listen” and “put under an oath” as “bound … under a curse.”
NASB follows the critical text; “dismissed” is rendered “let … go.”
NASB reorders the verse, moving “by the third hour of the night” forward, and adds “Get … ready.”
NASB turns the participle into a new sentence with “They were also to provide.”
NASB follows the critical text. A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; “seized” is rendered “arrested,” and “having come up with the troop” is “I came upon them with the troops.”
NASB follows the critical text; “to know” is rendered “to ascertain.”
NASB renders “chains” as “imprisonment.”
NASB follows the critical text without “by the Jews” and “Farewell”; “was being disclosed” is rendered “was informed.”
